question:
A uniform copper rod of length $L$ and cross-sectional area $A$ is pivoted at one end at the center of a fixed conducting circular ring of radius $L$. The free end of the rod maintains sliding contact with the ring, forming a closed circuit (ring resistance and contact resistance are negligible compared to the rod).

A uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is perpendicular to the plane of rotation. An external agent maintains the rod at a **constant** angular speed $\omega$. Assume all Joule heat produced is retained in the rod (no heat loss), and the temperature rise is small so that material properties remain constant.

Given: electrical resistivity of copper $\rho_e$ (ohm-m), mass density $\rho_m$ (kg m$^{-3}$), and specific heat capacity $s$ (J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$).

Find the **initial rate of rise of temperature** $\left(\dfrac{dT}{dt}\right)_{t=0}$ of the rod.
